name: Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Epidermolysis Bullosa

criteria.description: Presence of skin blistering and erosions following minor trauma
Histopathology showing cleavage below the basement membrane zone
Immunofluorescence or genetic testing demonstrating type VII collagen abnormalities
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Clinical blistering plus histopathologic confirmation of subbasement membrane cleavage and demonstration of type VII collagen abnormality
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for COL7A1 mutations confirms diagnosis and subtype

occasional.symptomName: Anemia secondary to chronic blood loss
Ocular surface erosions and conjunctival scarring
Increased risk of squamous cell carcinoma in chronic wounds

laboratory: Anemia of chronic disease or iron deficiency
Elevated inflammatory markers in chronic wounds
genetic: Mutations in COL7A1 gene encoding type VII collagen
other: Immunofluorescence mapping showing reduced or absent type VII collagen
Electron microscopy demonstrating sublamina densa cleavage

distinguishingFeatures: Blistering occurs within the lamina lucida of the basement membrane
Mutations in genes encoding laminin-332 or integrins
Blistering occurs within the basal keratinocytes of the epidermis
Generally milder disease with less scarring
Mutations in keratin 5 or keratin 14 genes

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging non-healing ulcer in chronic wound (possible squamous cell carcinoma)
Severe esophageal strictures causing feeding difficulties
Signs of systemic infection or sepsis from infected skin lesions
references: Fine JD, et al. Inherited epidermolysis bullosa: updated recommendations on diagnosis and classification. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2014.
Uitto J, et al. Molecular genetics of dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa. Matrix Biol. 2016.
Orphanet: Dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa. Available at: https://www.orpha.net
